questions.scenario: A verbose request verifies TLS and receives HTTP 503 with an edge request ID. What has the evidence established?

options.text: An HTTP component returned service unavailability

questions.explanation: An HTTP status is application-layer evidence after transport and, for HTTPS, TLS. Correlate the responding component and request ID with upstream evidence. [RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html).

questions.scenario: A retry system may automatically repeat a request after a connection interruption. Which method is defined as safe and idempotent for retrieving a resource?
questions.explanation: GET is a safe retrieval method and is idempotent. POST and PATCH can change state; CONNECT establishes a tunnel. [RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-methods).

questions.scenario: A monitor requests HTTP and records 308 with a Location header, while browsers work. What should the monitor do to test the final resource?

options.text: Follow the redirect and record both the redirect and final status

questions.explanation: A redirect instructs the client to use another URI. Following it tests the final endpoint while retaining the original redirection evidence. [RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-redirection-3xx).

questions.scenario: A client verifies an HTTPS server certificate. TCP has already connected to a shared endpoint. Which two identity and trust checks are essential?

options.text: The requested hostname matches a certificate identity
The chain reaches a trusted issuer and is within its validity interval

questions.explanation: Certificate verification checks identity, trust chain, and validity. A port number and later HTTP status do not authenticate the peer. [RFC 6125](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6125.html), [RFC 5280](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html).

questions.scenario: Several domains share one IP and port. The wrong certificate appears only when a legacy probe omits the hostname during TLS setup. Which mechanism is missing?
questions.explanation: Server Name Indication carries the intended hostname during TLS negotiation so a shared endpoint can select the right certificate. [RFC 6066](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6066.html).

questions.scenario: A TLS trace says the server accepted h2. Certificate verification also succeeded. What did ALPN negotiate?

options.text: The application protocol used inside the protected connection

questions.explanation: ALPN lets peers select an application protocol such as HTTP/2 during TLS. It does not choose DNS, routing, or certificate trust. [RFC 7301](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7301.html).

questions.scenario: A cached representation has ETag "release-42". The client sends If-None-Match with that value and receives 304. What should it do?

options.text: Treat the response as a missing route
Reuse the cached representation because it is still valid

questions.explanation: 304 indicates that the selected representation has not changed for the supplied validator, so the client can reuse its cached body. [RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-304-not-modified).

questions.scenario: A session cookie should travel only over HTTPS and should not be readable through browser JavaScript. Which two attributes address those requirements?
questions.explanation: Secure limits cookie transmission to secure channels, and HttpOnly restricts non-HTTP APIs such as script access. [RFC 6265](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6265.html).

questions.scenario: A browser blocks a cross-origin API response, but curl receives HTTP 200. Which boundary should be inspected?

options.text: The API's CORS response policy for the browser origin

questions.explanation: CORS is enforced by browsers using response headers and request origin context. A successful curl response does not prove the browser policy permits access. [Fetch standard](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/).

questions.scenario: The browser-to-proxy TLS handshake succeeds, but proxy logs show its upstream TLS verification fails. What does the browser success prove?

options.text: Only the client-facing TLS boundary succeeded
The backend certificate is trusted by the proxy

questions.explanation: TLS can terminate and begin again at separate hops. Evidence from one boundary does not establish trust or success at the next. [RFC 8446](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html).
